facts.statement: Fossils of Aprosuchus were discovered in the Pui Gater locality within the Hateg Basin of modern-day Transylvania, Romania.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in Maastrichtian sediments of the Pui Gater locality in the Hateg Basin in modern day Transylvania, Romania.

facts.statement: The genus is known from an incomplete skull and mandibles (holotype UBB V.562/1) and a cervical vertebra found nearby (referred specimen UBB V.562/2).
facts.quote: Aprosuchus is known from an incomplete three-dimensional skull and closely associated mandibles (Holotype UBB V.562/1) as well as a cervical vertebrae found in association with the cranial remains (referred specimen UBB V.562/2).

facts.statement: The name Aprosuchus combines the Hungarian word for 'small' and the Ancient Greek word for 'crocodile'.
facts.quote: The name derives from the Hungarian "apró" meaning small and the Ancient Greek σοῦχος, soukhos ("crocodile").

facts.statement: The species name ghirai was chosen to honor Ioan Ghira of Babeș-Bolyai University for his work in herpetology.
facts.quote: The species name ghirai honors Ioan Ghira from the Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, for his contributions to Herpetology.

facts.statement: The genus Aprosuchus was described by Venczel and Codrea in 2019.
Aprosuchus was a small-bodied crocodile relative that lived during the Maastrichtian stage in the Hateg Basin of Romania.
facts.quote: Aprosuchus is a genus of small-bodied Maastrichtian atoposaurid Eusuchian from the Hateg Basin, Romania.

facts.statement: Aprosuchus is distinguished by large eyelids fused to the skull bones and a mix of different tooth shapes.
facts.quote: It differs from other crocodylomorphs through large palpebral strongly fused to the orbital margin of the prefrontals and frontals and partly overlapping the prefrontal and lacrimal and heterodont dentition.

facts.statement: The teeth of Aprosuchus include at least four distinct types: pseudocaniniforms, two types of lanceolate teeth, and low-crowned teeth.
facts.quote: Aprosuchus dentition preserves at least four different morphotypes, pseudocaniniforms, pseudoziphodont lanceolate, ziphodont lanceolate and 'low-crowned' teeth.

facts.statement: A unique feature of Aprosuchus is the W-shaped overlap between its nasal and prefrontal bones, distinguishing it from Sabresuchus.
facts.quote: A further autapomorphy is the w-shaped overlap between the nasals and prefrontals which differentiates Aprosuchus from Sabresuchus symplesiodon.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the small Aprosuchus likely fed on invertebrates and small vertebrates.
facts.quote: In this ecosystem the small bodied Aprosuchus would have most likely preyed on invertebrates and small vertebrates.

facts.statement: The existence of Aprosuchus indicates that atoposaurid lineages survived into the Late Cretaceous by inhabiting island ecosystems in the Eastern Tethys.
facts.quote: The presence of Aprosuchus suggests that survivors of the Late Jurassic/Early Cretaceous atoposaurid lineage managed to survive up to the Late Cretaceous by colonising complex island ecosystems in the archipelagos of the Eastern Tethys.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Aprosuchus closely related to other atoposaurids, distinct from Wannchampsus and the Glen Rose Form.
facts.quote: They recovered that Aprosuchus ghirai appeared to be closely allied to other atoposaurids while Wannchampsus and the Glen Rose Form stood outside of the clade, but still closer to atoposaurids than to paralligatorids.

facts.statement: Aprosuchus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Aprosuchus belongs to the family Atoposauridae.
Aprosuchus is classified as a reptile.
The variety of tooth shapes in Aprosuchus raises questions about using teeth alone to identify atoposaurid genera beyond the family level.
facts.quote: The presence of four different tooth morphotypes casts doubt over the identification of atoposaurids based on teeth beyond a family level.

rejected.statement: Aprosuchus was a short-snouted crocodile relative with an estimated body length of 600 mm.
rejected.quote: Aprosuchus was a small sized brevirostrine Eusuchian with an estimated body length of 600 mm.
